text: That duration and green phlegm suggest an infection or chronic inflammation. Have you noticed any fever, night sweats, or unintended weight loss recently? Also, do you have a history of smoking or exposure to dust or chemicals?

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; the combination of a 25-year smoking history and daily exposure to mechanical dust significantly increases your risk for chronic lung conditions. text: RESULTS: Chest X-Ray: Hyperinflated lungs with increased anterior-posterior diameter, no evidence of infiltrates or masses. Spirometry: FEV1 65% of predicted, FVC 78% of predicted, FEV1/FVC Ratio 0.60 (reduced).

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray and spirometry results strongly suggest Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), likely with an acute exacerbation given the green phlegm. speaker: Doctor
text: The arterial blood gas results are reassuring, indicating your oxygenation is currently stable. speaker: Doctor
text: The improvement when you step away from dust suggests your symptoms are partially reversible, which can sometimes be seen in asthma, but your smoking history and spirometry strongly point to COPD.
